rationale: Structure: all 9 required sections present with clear headings. Faithfulness: multiple fabricated quotes (e.g., 'Memory is the one place...') and unsupported details (log.md) violate source. Coverage: captures key topics, stats, workflows, provider list. Precision: strong concrete numbers/names (13.5k stars, 24% search reduction, OKF fields, Mermaid) but includes unsupported log.md and vague unsupported claims. Compression: highly repetitive (benchmark stats repeated across topic map, key points, examples, summary; 'Why It Matters' boilerplate) and verbose.
hallucinations: "Memory is the one place where we felt the pain daily, could judge the output ourselves, and had a clear signal for whether it worked." — Brace Sproul (`00:39`)
"None of this works if generating the wiki is itself a project." — Brace Sproul (`01:42`)
"The interesting part is deciding not to run it... If you haven't made any changes, we don't need to update the repo." — Brace Sproul (`14:04`)
Codebase documentation is the ideal starting domain for general-purpose memory because ground truth is verifiable and developer pain is acute.
If generating and maintaining documentation requires manual developer overhead, adoption drops to zero.
openwiki/index.md: Root index declaring specification format and top-level links.
log.md / last-update.json: Changelog tracking codebase evolution.
updates only affected documentation modules, and updates log.md
Stale documentation causes AI hallucinations and incorrect code edits.
Agents fail when critical context is split across multiple conversational turns without explicit references.
A tool call accidentally returning a 50,000-token base64 image string into an LLM context window.
Configure `openwiki --update` inside your GitHub Actions CI/CD to run on schedule (e.g., daily cron) or on merge to main.
General-purpose memory for agents is finally viable due to modern long-context LLMs and agentic architectures.
